title: Finish Pocket
prompt:
Pocket is almost done: the state, `update`, `render`, storage and the add form all work. Wire up the last three pieces:

1. `visibleExpenses()` returns only the expenses whose `category` matches `state.filter`, or all of them when the filter is `"all"`. `render` already uses it for the list and the total.
2. When the `#filter` select changes, update the filter.
3. Add **one** delegated click listener on `#expense-list` that deletes the expense whose Delete button was clicked.

Change data only through `update(...)`, so every change is saved and re-rendered.
hints: `visibleExpenses` is one `if` and one `filter`: `state.expenses.filter((e) => e.category === state.filter)`.

For delete: `const button = event.target.closest(".delete"); if (!button) return;` then read `button.closest("li").dataset.id` and call `update({ expenses: state.expenses.filter((e) => e.id !== id) })`.
explanation: All three features are small because the structure does the heavy lifting. The filter is not stored anywhere except `state.filter`; the visible list and its total are derived from it at render time, so they can never disagree. The filter and delete handlers only work out new values and call `update`, which applies them, saves to storage and re-renders, so the saved data is always what the user sees. Delegation means the delete listener keeps working through every re-render and for newly added expenses. Because `idCounter` starts after the highest saved id, new expenses never reuse an id that is already stored.

checks.initial: Shows the three saved expenses and their total
checks.filter: Choosing Food shows only food expenses and their total
checks.delete: Deleting removes the expense from the page and from storage
checks.empty-state: A filter with no matches shows the empty message and $0.00
checks.add-and-all: Adding an expense with the filter on All shows it and saves it with a new id
